exposure: trophoectoderm (TE) biopsy for preimplantation genetic testing (PGT)
outcome: serum b-human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) level on the 15th day of embryo transfer (ET)
birthweight (average, probability of birth weight <=1500g, 1500-2500g, or <=2500g)
cohort: The study included women who delivered a singleton baby following frozen-thawed embryo transfer cycles, comparing those whose embryos underwent preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) with those who did not.
finding: Trophoectoderm biopsy was associated with a significantly lower average birth weight but did not seem to impact serum b-hCG levels or significantly increase the risk of preterm birth after adjusting for covariates.
